Telegram requires every client to carry an app key before it will send a login code, so a key is always needed. Vmore carries the keys open-source Telegram clients publish: it starts with the one that worked on this phone before, tries the others in turn, and stops the moment the login code is on its way. If Telegram refuses them all, your own api_id and api_hash above always work.

Vmore is a downloader and uploader that runs entirely on this phone.

1. Sign in once with your Telegram number and the login code. Nothing is sent to any server.
2. Paste a Telegram link on the home screen. Private links (t.me/c/…) work with your own account.
3. Choose the chat that should receive the files.
4. Tap Start. Vmore downloads the media and uploads it to that chat with your own data.

Ranges and batches: a range link such as t.me/channel/1-500 becomes one job per message, so a whole album or a whole channel section can be moved in one go. A link with no message in it (t.me/channel, or @channel) queues that chat's recent files, one job each.

Quality: sending as File keeps the original bytes. Video plays inline. Photo is a fast preview.

Storage: when Delete local copy is on, the phone copy is removed right after a successful upload and the job moves on to the next one.

All of this happens again by itself if the app is closed, because the queue runs as a foreground service.

Filters and duplicates: Settings can keep only the kinds you want and only a size range, and a file that was uploaded before is left out instead of being sent twice.

Data saving: Only on Wi-Fi, Only while charging and a download cap all hold the queue and let it go by themselves when the phone is ready.

Schedule: set a time in Settings and the queue begins by itself, once or every day. Start always means now.

While it works: Queue shows every job with pause, retry, priority arrows and remove. Retry all failed puts a whole batch back in line. History keeps everything.

Files and statistics: the Library opens the files on this phone (search, sort, upload again, share, delete), and Statistics adds up everything that moved through it.

Player and editor: speed from 0.25x to 3x, picture-in-picture, the next file by itself, trim, cover, remove sound and take the sound out as its own file.

When something fails: Vmore retries a job up to four times, and every retry asks Telegram for the link again, so a temporary refusal is not the end of the job. A chat that protects its content cannot be forwarded, so Vmore downloads the file and sends it as a copy. Only a real dead end stops early — a chat this account may not read, no room on the phone, a message that is gone — and the queue says which one it was. Settings, Check the Telegram connection, shows the last steps the queue took, and the whole report can be copied in one tap.
 a PIN lock guards the app, Day and Night are one tap apart, and up to three Telegram accounts can each keep their own session on this phone.

Clear everything: Settings, App data, Clear all app data empties the queue, the history, the downloaded files, the statistics and every account in one tap, and the app returns to its first-run sign-in.

Widget and tile: the home-screen widget and the Quick Settings tile pause or resume the queue without opening the app.
